statement: A hiking club has $160$ members, and each member prefers either mountain trails or coastal trails. Of the members, $70$ are under $40$ years old and the rest are $40$ or older. A total of $55$ members prefer mountain trails, and $30$ of those are under $40$. A member who is $40$ or older is chosen at random. What is the probability that this member prefers coastal trails?

choices.misconception: I found the 25 older members who prefer mountain trails and divided by 90, which answers the opposite preference.
I found the 65 older members who prefer coastal trails but divided by all 160 members instead of the 90 who are 40 or older.
I divided the 65 older coastal fans by the 105 members who prefer coastal trails, which reverses the condition.

hints: Build a two-way table with age group and trail preference, and fill in what you can.
There are $160 - 70 = 90$ members who are $40$ or older, and $55 - 30 = 25$ of the mountain fans are in that group.
So $90 - 25 = 65$ older members prefer coastal trails. The chosen member comes from the $90$ older members.

solutions.reliable: Members $40$ or older: $160 - 70 = 90$. Mountain fans who are $40$ or older: $55 - 30 = 25$. So $90 - 25 = 65$ of the older members prefer coastal trails. Given the member is $40$ or older, the probability is $\dfrac{65}{90} = \dfrac{13}{18}$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
